module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 21003

Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/21003](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003)
asked by user [*Z.H.*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/5098/z-h)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Polynomial


namespace Mathoverflow21003

/--
Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
theorem mathoverflow_21003 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ, Function.Bijective fun x ↦ f.eval x := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow21003

sources_consulted: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003 — original question, all three answers, and comments.
Giulio Bresciani, A higher dimensional Hilbert irreducibility theorem, arXiv:2101.01090, introduction and Theorem C; LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/2101.01090.
Bjorn Poonen, Multivariable polynomial injections on rational numbers, arXiv:0902.3961, abstract, Theorem 1.1, and introductory remarks; LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/0902.3961.
review.notes: The sole declaration, Mathoverflow21003.mathoverflow_21003, faithfully poses the source's existence question. MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ represents ℚ[x,y], and Lean infers the evaluation function's type as (Fin 2 → ℚ) → ℚ. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved its bijectivity equivalent to bijectivity on ℚ × ℚ, expanded the injectivity and surjectivity quantifiers, and checked zero, constant, projection, and sample polynomial evaluations. All checks compiled successfully without using the problem's sorry proof. The answer slot has the correct scope and affirmative polarity. The source records conditional progress, not an unconditional resolution: Bresciani's nonexistence theorem assumes weak Bombieri–Lang for surfaces, while Poonen's conditional result concerns injections. Thus research open remains consistent with the consulted sources.
